title: Ultrasonic pretreatment-induced conformational alteration of large yellow croaker bone protein: enhanced osteogenic activity of enzymatic hydrolysates and molecular insights.
authors: Feng, Jun; Jing, Ziqian; Liang, Xinyi; Kang, Wenrui; Du, Ming; Wang, Zhenyu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究超声预处理改变鱼骨蛋白构象并增强酶解产物成骨活性，涉及分子对接和MD模拟，但核心对象为食品蛋白水解物而非蛋白质结构计算建模，方法贡献较弱。
abstract: Ultrasound pretreatment is increasingly used to modulate protein conformation and facilitate the release of bioactive peptides for functional food applications. In this study, large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) bone proteins were subjected to ultrasound pretreatment to investigate the relationship among ultrasound-induced protein conformational changes, enzymatic hydrolysis behavior, and the osteogenic activity of the resulting hydrolysates. Ultrasonic treatment at 300 W significantly altered protein conformation, increased the accessibility of neutral protease, and consequently enhanced both the degree of hydrolysis and the proportion of low-molecular-weight peptides. Hydrolysates produced under this condition exhibited the highest osteogenic activity, as evidenced by increased MC3T3-E1 cell proliferation, alkaline phosphatase activity, and mineralized nodule formation. LC-MS/MS analysis combined with molecular docking-based virtual screening proposed three proline-rich peptides, GPPGPMGPPG, GPSGPVGP, and APDPGPGP, as candidate osteogenic peptides. Refined molecular docking predicted favorable interactions of all three peptides with the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). The 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation further supported the stability of the representative GPPGPMGPPG-EGFR complex. Altogether, ultrasound pretreatment facilitates the generation of low-molecular-weight peptide-rich hydrolysates with enhanced osteogenic potential from fish bone proteins. These findings provide a feasible strategy for valorizing marine by-products into functional food ingredients for bone health management.
abstract_zh: 超声预处理越来越多地被用于调节蛋白质构象并促进生物活性肽的释放，以应用于功能性食品。本研究对大黄鱼（Larimichthys crocea）骨蛋白进行超声预处理，以探讨超声诱导的蛋白质构象变化、酶解行为及所得水解产物成骨活性之间的关系。300 W超声处理显著改变了蛋白质构象，增加了中性蛋白酶的可及性，从而提高了水解度和低分子量肽的比例。在此条件下产生的水解产物表现出最高的成骨活性，表现为MC3T3-E1细胞增殖、碱性磷酸酶活性和矿化结节形成的增加。LC-MS/MS分析结合基于分子对接的虚拟筛选提出了三种富含脯氨酸的肽，即GPPGPMGPPG、GPSGPVGP和APDPGPGP，作为候选成骨肽。精细化分子对接预测了所有三种肽与表皮生长因子受体（EGFR）的有利相互作用。100 ns分子动力学模拟进一步支持了代表性GPPGPMGPPG-EGFR复合物的稳定性。总体而言，超声预处理促进了从鱼骨蛋白中生成富含低分子量肽且具有增强成骨潜力的水解产物。这些发现为将海洋副产物转化为用于骨骼健康管理的功能性食品成分提供了一种可行策略。
